items.title: Housing market seeing 'rapid deterioration' as downturn deepens
items.description: Australia's housing downturn is spreading across the country, with the latest property price data showing previously resilient markets that had recently set record-high prices are now experiencing a decline in values.

items.title: Single mum has front-row seat to first home buyer struggles
items.description: Tess McKenna is an example of how hard it is to find an affordable home in Perth, saying it is not getting easier despite the market cooling.

items.title: Global shockwaves as South Korea's crash rattles markets
items.description: Balance is a fundamental principle of everyday life on the Korean peninsula, but the worst stock market crash in the nation's history threatens the livelihood of millions.

items.title: Ex-NRL player reveals drug offers during crippling gambling addiction
items.description: Luke Bateman says gambling company employees unofficially offered him illicit drugs in order to cultivate a relationship with him when he was high-spend punter.

items.title: In a remote community, a boy asked me a question no child should
items.description: In the tiny community of Baniyala, in East Arnhem Land, I sat next to a 13-year-old boy who asked me a question no child should be asking.

items.title: 'The public is being duped': What that logo on your chocolate actually guarantees
items.description: For decades, major chocolate companies have pledged to eradicate child labour. Four Corners discovered that in Ghana, the promises don't always match the reality.

items.title: Kellie Sloane needs clear air, but ICAC claims are starving her of oxygen
items.description: This week, ICAC's gaze is likely to feel even closer for state opposition leader Kellie Sloane, as the anti-corruption commission hears from one of her most senior parliamentary colleagues.

items.title: Iranians say the regime is at war 'with its own people'
items.description: Three Iranians have shared their insights on life under the regime, as the war passes its fifth month and US President Donald Trump threatens a return to all-out fighting if no long-term peace deal can be struck.

items.title: Quick hits: Delta stuns with Aussie classic, 76yo claims history-making gold
items.description: Delta Goodrem belts out an Aussie classic, a 76-year-old makes Commonwealth Games history and a cycling star is proud to have not thrown up on the podium. Here are the quick hits from the final day of the Commonwealth Games.

items.title: Live: ASX set to tumble despite Wall St rallying on Amazon earnings
items.description: The ASX is priced for a sharp decline this morning despite Wall Street rallying strongly on Friday. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Live: Big tech faces higher tax if it does not reach deals with local publishers
items.description: Tech companies will be forced to pay a 2.5 per cent tax on digital advertising revenue if they do not reach deals with media companies. Follow live.

items.title: Two Australian helicopters collide midair fighting fires in Greece
items.description: Two firefighters are dead after a collision between two helicopters near Athens, as Europe's wildfire emergency continues.

items.title: Queensland woman forced to ask for exemption to use her own embryos
items.description: Several women were told they could no longer proceed with their treatments after the release of the Queensland Health guidance earlier this year.

items.title: Citizenship rule takes effect amid spike in Qld gun licence applications
items.description: New restrictions on who can own guns in Queensland come into effect today, amid a spike in new applications to register weapons.

items.title: Vehicle with 1 million kilometres on the clock hits the market
items.description: A west Victorian stock agent lists his 2009 Toyota LandCruiser for sale, having driven it 300 metres shy of 1 million kilometres.

items.title: Constantly being asked to perform duties outside of your job description? Read this
items.description: Individual employment contracts often include a clause that says an employee may be required to undertake other duties as required, but what is fair and reasonable depends on a few things.

items.title: Race Around the World recap: Catch this week's films
items.description: From pagan ceremonies to the world's biggest data centre, catch up on every week nine film from Race Around the World.

items.title: Safety concerns for ex-ASIO agent as he seeks visa to testify
items.description: It is the former agent's second bid to enter Australia after his first visa was rejected because immigration authorities feared he was unlikely to leave.

items.title: Tasmania's greyhound racing ban closer, some trainers keen on exit scheme
items.description: As legislation to ban greyhound racing in Tasmanian remains stalled, a handful of racing participants have expressed interest in joining a compensation scheme to leave the industry.

items.title: Ben Carroll to fill one of three vacancies in Victorian cabinet, ABC understands
items.description: MPs tell the ABC Victoria's new premier is only expected to fill one of the three vacancies in cabinet.

items.title: Blues pay tribute to 'hero' Daley as he stands down as coach
items.description: The NSWRL pays tribute to Blues "hero" Laurie Daley as the coach stands down from his role after this year's series win over Queensland.

items.title: Morocco blames social media, human traffickers for Spain migrant rush
items.description: Morocco's Interior Ministry says at least 11 people died, most by drowning, while trying to cross the border into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, in a rush of about 40,000 people blamed by the government on social media misinformation and human trafficking networks.

items.title: Trump holds off on new strikes against Iran amid emerging 'deal'
items.description: Donald Trump says the US will hold off on fresh strikes against Iran, as Middle East allies have agreed to parameters of a deal to end the war.

items.title: Residents hope to raise $750,000 to fix small town's aged care problem
items.description: Residents in Texas are kept awake at night wondering what will happen to them as they get older, but they are dreaming big.

items.title: Staff get 52 long weekends a year as council trials four-day work week
items.description: In an Australian first, Murrumbidgee Council staff will get long weekends every week from next year when a four-day working week trial begins.
